Q1.question: What does 'accelerating expansion' mean when time is the count of record-events?
Q1.ruling: D1 and D2 agree and both are right; LC agrees. Under PD-35 and PD-37, with PD-20 (one site is one record-event) and a steady written share (PD-36; PD-42, principal), elapsed time t is proportional to the site count N (constant factors from PD-11, PD-27 and PD-38 drop out). The creation rate per unit of this time is fixed by construction (about one site per record-event): it can neither rise nor fall. The expansion rate is H_t = dlnD/dt for old-pair distances D; expansion rate times age is dlnD/dlnt = gamma exactly (gamma (1 - N0/N) if age is counted from the first growth). Speeding up means D convex in t: q_t = -1 + 1/gamma - (dgamma/dln t)/gamma^2 < 0, i.e. dgamma/dln t > gamma (1 - gamma), which is 0.166 / 0.1875 / 0.206 per e-fold of the count at gamma 0.21 / 0.25 / 0.29; for a steady law gamma > 1, old distances outgrowing the count itself.
Q1.hand_rederivation: t = cN. ln D = INT gamma dln t, so D_t = gamma D/t and D_tt = D (gamma' + gamma^2 - gamma)/t^2 with gamma' = dgamma/dln t. Then q_t = -D D_tt/D_t^2 = -(gamma' + gamma^2 - gamma)/gamma^2 = -1 + 1/gamma - gamma'/gamma^2. Checked numerically (R5).
Q1.the_coordinators_caveat: As worded ('the creation rate rising faster than the surface') it has no content in PD-37's clock: the creation rate is the clock's own unit. It is the speeding-up condition beta > 1 - gamma of a clock in which each growth point, or any local process, runs at a steady rate (batch-7 T1 corrections (i) and (iv), checked; batch-6 TR step 8, checked); it reads 2/3 ('the surface') only at gamma = 1/3, and 3/4 at the measured 1/4. Its parenthesis ('batch 7: it does under every event tested') is true as a fact about beta (about 1 for every event; PD-17 0.96-1.19, H122 check C1), but beta drops out of count-time expansion entirely. Correct form under PD-37: old distances must grow faster than the count of record-events itself, which no network can keep doing (Q2). In the principal's own words (0303): in this clock 'record expansion' runs at exactly one record-event per tick for ever, so it can never be 'accelerating'.

Q2.ruling: RIGHT IN SUBSTANCE AND STRONGER THAN STATED, WITH FOUR CORRECTIONS (D1 and D2 agree; every step re-derived by the referee).
corrections: (a) No lasting speed-up needs neither three dimensions nor constant density. In any connected network a hop distance is at most N - 1 (a shortest path visits distinct sites; Births keep the network connected), and N <= t/c, so D/t stays bounded. If q stayed below some -e < 0, then D' >= C D^e and D would grow at least as t^(1/(1-e)), superlinear, which the bound forbids. Only a network that is one-dimensional on the old pairs' scale can approach steady coasting from below (D = t - sqrt t). Batch-6 TR step 7 and its check C2 (checked) already state this for a Births or all-moves clock; under PD-20 and a steady written share the record-event clock is such a clock up to a constant.

(b) While the program's three-dimensional label holds (rho = mean eccentricity of 16 seeded centres / 2(N/2)^(1/3) <= 1.5; batch4 scripts_copied/r1/FROZEN_R1.txt), every pair distance <= the diameter <= 2 x the smallest eccentricity <= 2 x the mean eccentricity <= 6 x 2^(-1/3) N^(1/3) = 4.76 N^(1/3) (D2's step; re-derived by the triangle inequality; constant checked, R4). So the long-run average rate times age is at most 1/3; about 1/4 on the whole-history reading (PD-39's second grade; batch-15 S20, checked; batch-11 FL's checked identity: a body that keeps its shape has stretch x ball slope = 1).

(c) 'Would slow' should read 'cannot keep speeding up, and slows on average'. A brief speed-up is not excluded (TR check C2; D1 T4; D2 C1). Quantified here (registered before code, held): a convex D(t) under the label's cap must stop speeding up within a factor x* of the count. Swinging from the compact edge of the label to its stretched edge (rho 0.67 to 1.5) gives x* = 31 / 22 / 17 for an initial rate times age of 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.30 (about 4-5 doublings), during which old distances must grow at an average exponent of 0.57-0.62, about twice the largest value on file, and the episode must then be repaid by slowing (afterwards the cap forces exponent <= 1/3 on average). Pairs that start on the cap get only x* = 3.8 / 2.2 / 1.4. Post-test, no credit: typical pairs well inside the diameter cap (f = 0.17) could run x* = 153 / 110 / 83 with average exponent 0.69-0.73. Any speed-up at all needs the exponent to climb by more than 0.17-0.21 per e-fold of the count; no checked body shows a rising exponent.

(d) It is a statement about count time only. Exactly, for any clock tau with R = dt/dtau: q_count = q_local + dlnR/dlnD (D1's S6; re-derived: D_t = D_tau/R, D_tt = (D_tautau R - D_tau R_tau)/R^3; numeric gap 5e-6, R1 v2). Whenever the whole network makes more record-events per local tick as it grows, the count reads more decelerating than any local clock.

A network that stays three-dimensional slows on average, and every tested network slows: old distances grow as about the 0.2 to 0.3 power of the count. But no piece of the network can see that count; a clock can only count what happens near it. Counted near a piece, the same networks speed up, because new growth points keep pace with the network. Even the standard picture of our own universe, with record-events spread evenly through space and time, would look as if it were slowing in the whole-network count (recalled). Which count a clock keeps is your question. One model family.

plain_summary: Referee ruling, dark energy. The tension is confirmed: if elapsed time is the count of record-events over the whole network, expansion can never keep speeding up unless the network is a single thread; a three-dimensional network slows on average, and every tested network slows. The caveat recorded with that decision cannot work there: record creation runs at exactly one per tick. So on today's clock the card is against, but the fault is the clock, not the growth: no piece of the network can see that count, and even our own universe would look as if it were slowing in it (recalled). A count of record-events near a piece speeds up on every steadily stretching network tested, while the whole-network count stays the network's time. Costs: speeding up from the start, no earlier slowing era, no predicted rate yet. One question goes to the principal. One model family.
